dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Good morning, Grand City Hotel. How can I help you today?

dialogue.speaker: Guest
dialogue.text: Hello, I would like to book a single room with breakfast for three nights starting this Friday.

question: What type of room does the guest want to book?
options: A single room with breakfast
A double room without meals
A family suite for a week
A shared dormitory bed
audioText: Receptionist: Good morning, Grand City Hotel. How can I help you today? Guest: Hello, I would like to book a single room with breakfast for three nights starting this Friday. Question: What type of room does the guest want to book?
translation:
직원: 안녕하세요, 그랜드 시티 호텔입니다. 무엇을 도와드릴까요?
투숙객: 안녕하세요, 이번 주 금요일부터 3박 동안 조식이 포함된 싱글룸(a single room with breakfast)을 예약하고 싶습니다.
질문: 투숙객이 예약하고 싶어 하는 방은 어떤 유형인가?
tip: [Band 5.0 · Listening Sec 1] 핵심 명사구 "a single room with breakfast"를 그대로 듣고 답을 고르는 기초 문제입니다.

dialogue.speaker: Librarian
dialogue.text: To make a new library card, I need to see an ID with your photo, such as a passport or student card.

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.text: Here is my university student card right in my wallet.

question: What does the student show to the librarian?
options: A university student card
An electricity bill
A bank statement
A train ticket
audioText: Librarian: To make a new library card, I need to see an ID with your photo, such as a passport or student card. Student: Here is my university student card right in my wallet. Question: What does the student show to the librarian?
translation:
사서: 새 도서관 카드를 만들려면 여권이나 학생증처럼 사진이 있는 신분증을 보여주셔야 합니다.
학생: 제 지갑에 대학교 학생증(university student card)이 여기 있습니다.
질문: 학생이 사서에게 보여준 것은 무엇인가?
tip: [Band 5.0 · Listening Sec 1] 사서가 예시로 든 여권/학생증 중 학생이 실제로 제시한 "university student card"를 선택합니다.

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.text: We have a small city car for forty dollars a day, or a large van for seventy dollars.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: We have four big suitcases, so we definitely need the large van.

question: Why did the customer choose the large van?
options: They have four big suitcases
The small car was already booked
The van had a special discount
They are traveling with eight people
audioText: Agent: We have a small city car for forty dollars a day, or a large van for seventy dollars. Customer: We have four big suitcases, so we definitely need the large van. Question: Why did the customer choose the large van?
translation:
직원: 하루 40달러짜리 소형 시내 차량과 70달러짜리 대형 밴이 있습니다.
고객: 큰 여행가방이 4개나 있어서 무조건 대형 밴이 필요합니다.
질문: 고객이 대형 밴을 선택한 이유는 무엇인가?
tip: [Band 5.0 · Listening Sec 1] 이유를 나타내는 "We have four big suitcases, so ~" 부분을 정확히 청취합니다.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: We have beginner swimming classes on Tuesday evenings and Saturday mornings.

dialogue.speaker: Member
dialogue.text: I work late on weekdays, so the Saturday morning class is best for me.

question: When will the member attend the swimming class?
options: On Saturday mornings
On Tuesday evenings
On Friday afternoons
Every weekday morning
audioText: Receptionist: We have beginner swimming classes on Tuesday evenings and Saturday mornings. Member: I work late on weekdays, so the Saturday morning class is best for me. Question: When will the member attend the swimming class?
translation:
안내원: 초급 수영 수업은 화요일 저녁과 토요일 오전에 있습니다.
회원: 평일에는 늦게까지 일해서 토요일 오전 수업이 저에게 가장 좋겠네요.
질문: 회원은 언제 수영 수업에 참석할 예정인가?
tip: [Band 5.0 · Listening Sec 1] 평일 야근 때문에 선택한 "Saturday morning class"를 포착합니다.

dialogue.speaker: Tour Guide
dialogue.text: The walking tour starts at the main square at nine-thirty, so please meet us ten minutes early at nine-twenty.

dialogue.speaker: Tourist
dialogue.text: Okay, we will be at the main square at nine-twenty.

question: What time should the tourists meet at the main square?
options: At 9:20 AM
At 9:30 AM
At 9:00 AM
At 10:00 AM
audioText: Tour Guide: The walking tour starts at the main square at nine-thirty, so please meet us ten minutes early at nine-twenty. Tourist: Okay, we will be at the main square at nine-twenty. Question: What time should the tourists meet at the main square?
translation:
가이드: 워킹 투어는 중앙 광장에서 9시 30분에 출발하니, 10분 일찍 9시 20분에 모여 주세요.
관광객: 네, 9시 20분까지 중앙 광장으로 가겠습니다.
질문: 관광객들이 중앙 광장에 모여야 하는 시간은 언제인가?
tip: [Band 5.0 · Listening Sec 1] 출발 시간(9:30)과 모이는 시간(9:20)을 구분하는 전형적인 시간 청취 문제입니다.

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: Now, turning to our university sports complex. Please note that while the gymnasium is open seven days a week, the Olympic swimming pool is currently closed for urgent maintenance.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: When is the pool expected to reopen to registered members?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: Technicians estimate work will finish by next Thursday morning.

question: Which facility is temporarily unavailable to visitors?
options: The Olympic swimming pool
The fitness gymnasium
The outdoor tennis courts
The campus cafeteria
audioText: Guide: Now, turning to our university sports complex. Please note that while the gymnasium is open seven days a week, the Olympic swimming pool is currently closed for urgent maintenance. Visitor: When is the pool expected to reopen to registered members? Guide: Technicians estimate work will finish by next Thursday morning. Question: Which facility is temporarily unavailable to visitors?
translation:
가이드: 이제 대학 스포츠 콤플렉스로 가보겠습니다. 체육관은 주 7일 운영되지만, 올림픽 규격 수영장은 현재 긴급 보수 공사로 문을 닫았으니 유의하시기 바랍니다.
방문객: 등록 회원들에게 수영장이 언제 다시 열릴 예정인가요?
가이드: 기사분들께서는 다음 주 목요일 아침까지 작업이 끝날 것으로 예상하고 있습니다.
질문: 방문객이 현재 일시적으로 이용할 수 없는 시설은 무엇인가?
tip: [Band 5.5~6.5 · Listening Sec 2] "currently closed for urgent maintenance"가 질문의 "temporarily unavailable"로 패러프레이징되었습니다.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.text: Your project outline looks good, David, but interviewing only ten students is too small a sample.

dialogue.speaker: David
dialogue.text: Should I send out an online survey to at least one hundred students instead?

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.text: Exactly. A larger online survey will make your final results much more reliable.

question: What does the tutor advise David to do for his project?
options: Survey a larger number of students online
Rewrite the introduction of his paper
Change his research topic completely
Cancel the student interviews immediately
answer: Survey a larger number of students online
audioText: Tutor: Your project outline looks good, David, but interviewing only ten students is too small a sample. David: Should I send out an online survey to at least one hundred students instead? Tutor: Exactly. A larger online survey will make your final results much more reliable. Question: What does the tutor advise David to do for his project?
translation:
지도교수: 데이비드, 프로젝트 개요는 좋지만 학생 10명만 인터뷰하는 건 표본이 너무 작네.
데이비드: 대신 최소 100명의 학생에게 온라인 설문지를 보내는 게 좋을까요?
지도교수: 맞아. 더 큰 규모의 온라인 설문조사를 하면 최종 결과가 훨씬 더 신뢰할 만해질 거야.
질문: 지도교수는 데이비드에게 프로젝트를 위해 무엇을 하라고 조언하는가?
tip: [Band 5.5~6.5 · Listening Sec 3] "send out an online survey to at least one hundred students"와 "A larger online survey"를 연결합니다.

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.text: Starting next month, plastic bottles and metal cans must be sorted into green bins, while cardboard packaging belongs exclusively in the blue container.

dialogue.speaker: Resident
dialogue.text: Where should broken glass and lightbulbs be discarded?

dialogue.speaker: Officer
dialogue.text: Glass items must be taken directly to the local depot rather than curbside collection.

question: Where should residents take discarded glass items?
options: Directly to the local municipal depot
Inside the curbside green bins
Inside the blue cardboard containers
Into the general household trash
answer: Directly to the local municipal depot
audioText: Officer: Starting next month, plastic bottles and metal cans must be sorted into green bins, while cardboard packaging belongs exclusively in the blue container. Resident: Where should broken glass and lightbulbs be discarded? Officer: Glass items must be taken directly to the local depot rather than curbside collection. Question: Where should residents take discarded glass items?
translation:
담당관: 다음 달부터 플라스틱병과 캔은 녹색 통에, 판지 포장재는 파란색 통에 분리수거해야 합니다.
주민: 깨진 유리와 백열전구는 어디에 버려야 하나요?
담당관: 유리 제품은 문 앞 수거 대신 지역 집하장으로 직접 가져가셔야 합니다.
질문: 주민들은 버려진 유리 제품을 어디로 가져가야 하는가?
tip: 색상 통(green/blue)은 플라스틱/판지용이며, 유리는 "taken directly to the local depot"임을 포착합니다.

dialogue.speaker: Sarah
dialogue.text: We only have fifteen minutes for the seminar presentation. Should we present every case study?

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: No, concentrating deeply on just two contrasting case studies will demonstrate much better critical analysis than rushing through five.

question: How do the students decide to structure their presentation?
options: Focusing deeply on two contrasting case studies
Presenting five quick case study overviews
Extending their talk to thirty minutes with the tutor
Replacing case studies with theoretical mathematical proofs
answer: Focusing deeply on two contrasting case studies
audioText: Sarah: We only have fifteen minutes for the seminar presentation. Should we present every case study? Tom: No, concentrating deeply on just two contrasting case studies will demonstrate much better critical analysis than rushing through five. Question: How do the students decide to structure their presentation?
translation:
사라: 세미나 발표 시간이 15분밖에 없어. 모든 사례 연구를 다 발표해야 할까?
톰: 아니, 5개를 서둘러 훑기보다는 대조적인 사례 연구 2개에 깊이 집중하는 편이 훨씬 더 나은 비판적 분석을 보여줄 거야.
질문: 학생들은 발표를 어떻게 구성하기로 결정했는가?
tip: "concentrating deeply on just two contrasting case studies"가 정답의 핵심 단서입니다.

dialogue.speaker: Curator
dialogue.text: The photography exhibit in the east wing requires timed entry tickets, whereas the permanent sculpture garden on the ground floor is open free of charge without booking.

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: Is flash photography allowed near the ancient textiles?

dialogue.speaker: Curator
dialogue.text: Flash is strictly prohibited everywhere inside the gallery to protect sensitive pigments.

question: What restriction is strictly enforced inside the museum galleries?
options: Flash photography is strictly prohibited
Visitors must wear special cotton gloves
Backpacks must be carried only by children
No liquids or water bottles allowed anywhere on the property
audioText: Curator: The photography exhibit in the east wing requires timed entry tickets, whereas the permanent sculpture garden on the ground floor is open free of charge without booking. Visitor: Is flash photography allowed near the ancient textiles? Curator: Flash is strictly prohibited everywhere inside the gallery to protect sensitive pigments. Question: What restriction is strictly enforced inside the museum galleries?
translation:
큐레이터: 동관 사진전은 시간제 입장권이 필요하지만, 1층 상설 조각 정원은 예약 없이 무료로 입장하실 수 있습니다.
방문객: 고대 직물 근처에서 플래시 촬영이 허용되나요?
큐레이터: 민감한 안료를 보호하기 위해 갤러리 내부 어디에서든 플래시는 엄격히 금지됩니다.
질문: 박물관 갤러리 내부에서 엄격히 시행되는 제한은 무엇인가?
tip: "Flash is strictly prohibited everywhere inside the gallery" 청취 후 직관적으로 답을 고릅니다.

dialogue.speaker: Professor
dialogue.text: Did you notice any unexpected anomalies during your soil acidity measurements in the northern quadrant?

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.text: Yes, the pH levels dropped dramatically near the industrial drainage canal, which distorted our baseline averages.

question: What caused the anomalous drop in soil pH readings?
options: Proximity to an industrial drainage canal
Heavy rainfall that diluted soil minerals
Defective laboratory testing equipment
Seasonal leaf decomposition on the surface
answer: Proximity to an industrial drainage canal
audioText: Professor: Did you notice any unexpected anomalies during your soil acidity measurements in the northern quadrant? Student: Yes, the pH levels dropped dramatically near the industrial drainage canal, which distorted our baseline averages. Question: What caused the anomalous drop in soil pH readings?
translation:
교수: 북쪽 구역 토양 산도 측정 중에 예상치 못한 변칙치가 있었나?
학생: 네, 산업 배수관 근처에서 pH 수치가 급격히 떨어져 기준선 평균이 왜곡되었습니다.
질문: 토양 pH 측정값의 이상 급락을 유발한 원인은 무엇인가?
tip: "near the industrial drainage canal"이 선택지에서 "Proximity to an industrial drainage canal"로 패러프레이징되었습니다.

dialogue.speaker: Professor
dialogue.text: Coral bleaching occurs predominantly when water temperatures rise beyond typical seasonal thresholds. Under prolonged thermal stress, corals expel the symbiotic algae inhabiting their tissues, causing them to turn completely white. Contrary to popular belief, bleached corals are not dead; however, their mortality rate increases substantially if environmental conditions do not normalize within several weeks.

question: What is the primary biological consequence when corals undergo severe thermal stress?
options: They expel microscopic symbiotic algae from their tissue
They permanently lose their physical calcium structure
They instantaneously perish within twenty-four hours
They rapidly migrate to deeper marine trenches
answer: They expel microscopic symbiotic algae from their tissue
audioText: Professor: Coral bleaching occurs predominantly when water temperatures rise beyond typical seasonal thresholds. Under prolonged thermal stress, corals expel the symbiotic algae inhabiting their tissues, causing them to turn completely white. Contrary to popular belief, bleached corals are not dead; however, their mortality rate increases substantially if environmental conditions do not normalize within several weeks. Question: What is the primary biological consequence when corals undergo severe thermal stress?
translation:
교수: 산호 백화 현상은 주로 수온이 일반적인 계절적 한계치를 초과하여 상승할 때 발생합니다. 장기간 열 스트레스를 받으면, 산호는 조직에 서식하는 공생 조류(algae)를 체외로 방출하여 완전히 하얗게 변합니다. 일반적인 믿음과 달리 백화된 산호가 곧바로 죽은 것은 아니지만, 몇 주 내에 환경 조건이 정상화되지 않으면 폐사율이 크게 증가합니다.
질문: 산호가 심각한 열 스트레스를 겪을 때 나타나는 주요 생물학적 결과는 무엇인가?
tip: 학술 강의 독백으로 "expel the symbiotic algae inhabiting their tissues"라는 과학적 인과 과정을 청취해야 합니다.

dialogue.speaker: Lecturer
dialogue.text: Recent cognitive experiments demonstrate that multitasking does not signify parallel processing capability. Instead, the brain rapidly toggles executive attention between disparate tasks, incurring a quantifiable cognitive switching cost that degrades both accuracy and long-term memory encoding.

question: What does the lecturer state regarding the reality of cognitive multitasking?
options: It involves rapid attention toggling that incurs cognitive switching costs
It genuinely enhances long-term memory retention and verbal fluency
It is a distinct neurological ability found solely in trained bilinguals
It eliminates mental fatigue when working on repetitive computational tasks
answer: It involves rapid attention toggling that incurs cognitive switching costs
audioText: Lecturer: Recent cognitive experiments demonstrate that multitasking does not signify parallel processing capability. Instead, the brain rapidly toggles executive attention between disparate tasks, incurring a quantifiable cognitive switching cost that degrades both accuracy and long-term memory encoding. Question: What does the lecturer state regarding the reality of cognitive multitasking?
translation:
강사: 최근의 인지 실험들은 멀티태스킹이 병렬 처리 능력을 의미하지 않는다는 점을 보여줍니다. 대신 뇌는 서로 다른 작업 간에 집행적 주의 집중을 빠르게 전환하며, 이 과정에서 정확도와 장기 기억 형성을 모두 저하시키는 측정 가능한 인지적 전환 비용(switching cost)을 발생시킵니다.
질문: 강사는 인지적 멀티태스킹의 실체에 대해 무엇이라고 언급하는가?
tip: "rapidly toggles executive attention"과 "cognitive switching cost" 핵심 학술 어구를 청취합니다.

dialogue.speaker: Professor
dialogue.text: The intermittent nature of solar and wind energy represents the foremost impediment to wholesale grid decarbonization. Consequently, grid operators are investing heavily in grid-scale vanadium redox flow batteries, which offer multi-hour storage capacity without degrading over tens of thousands of chemical cycles.

question: Why are grid operators specifically adopting vanadium redox flow batteries?
options: They provide multi-hour storage without cycle degradation
They are substantially cheaper than conventional lead-acid cells
They produce combustible hydrogen fuel as a useful byproduct
They do not require physical containment infrastructure
answer: They provide multi-hour storage without cycle degradation
audioText: Professor: The intermittent nature of solar and wind energy represents the foremost impediment to wholesale grid decarbonization. Consequently, grid operators are investing heavily in grid-scale vanadium redox flow batteries, which offer multi-hour storage capacity without degrading over tens of thousands of chemical cycles. Question: Why are grid operators specifically adopting vanadium redox flow batteries?
translation:
교수: 태양광과 풍력 에너지의 간헐적 특성은 전면적인 전력망 탈탄소화의 가장 큰 장애물입니다. 따라서 전력망 운영자들은 수만 번의 화학 주기 동안 열화되지 않고 수 시간 동안의 저장 용량을 제공하는 그리드 규모의 바나듐 레독스 흐름 전지에 막대한 투자를 진행하고 있습니다.
질문: 전력망 운영자들이 바나듐 레독스 흐름 전지를 특별히 도입하는 이유는 무엇인가?
tip: "multi-hour storage capacity without degrading over tens of thousands of chemical cycles" 문장을 선지의 "without cycle degradation"으로 연결합니다.

dialogue.speaker: Historian
dialogue.text: Contrary to earlier historiographical claims that Roman urban centers collapsed solely due to barbarian incursions, recent paleobotanical sediment core analysis reveals that chronic agricultural drought during the fifth century critically diminished grain reserves and undermined imperial logistics.

question: What new insight did paleobotanical sediment analysis uncover about the Roman collapse?
options: Chronic agricultural droughts severely depleted critical grain reserves
Hostile barbarian armies burned down agricultural grain depots
Urban populations abandoned cities due to catastrophic lead poisoning
Sea level fluctuations submerged Mediterranean naval supply harbors
answer: Chronic agricultural droughts severely depleted critical grain reserves
audioText: Historian: Contrary to earlier historiographical claims that Roman urban centers collapsed solely due to barbarian incursions, recent paleobotanical sediment core analysis reveals that chronic agricultural drought during the fifth century critically diminished grain reserves and undermined imperial logistics. Question: What new insight did paleobotanical sediment analysis uncover about the Roman collapse?
translation:
역사학자: 로마의 도시 중심지가 오로지 야만인의 침략으로 인해 붕괴했다는 과거 사학계의 주장과 달리, 최근의 고식물학적 퇴적물 코어 분석은 5세기 동안 지속된 만성 농업 가뭄이 식량 비축량을 심각하게 고갈시키고 제국의 병참을 약화시켰음을 밝혀냈습니다.
질문: 고식물학적 퇴적물 분석이 로마의 붕괴에 대해 밝혀낸 새로운 통찰은 무엇인가?
tip: 과거의 통념("barbarian incursions") 함정을 피하고, 새로운 발견인 "chronic agricultural drought ~ diminished grain reserves"를 선택합니다.

dialogue.speaker: Professor
dialogue.text: Convergent evolution demonstrates how unrelated organisms independently evolve strikingly similar physiological adaptations when exposed to equivalent environmental pressures. The streamlined fusiform bodies of dolphins and sharks offer classic morphological evidence of hydrodynamic optimization in marine environments.

question: What does the morphological similarity between dolphins and sharks exemplify?
options: Independent adaptation driven by convergent evolution
A direct common ancestral link within recent evolutionary history
Artificial selective breeding implemented by human coastal societies
Genetic mutation caused by high aquatic hydrostatic pressure
answer: Independent adaptation driven by convergent evolution
audioText: Professor: Convergent evolution demonstrates how unrelated organisms independently evolve strikingly similar physiological adaptations when exposed to equivalent environmental pressures. The streamlined fusiform bodies of dolphins and sharks offer classic morphological evidence of hydrodynamic optimization in marine environments. Question: What does the morphological similarity between dolphins and sharks exemplify?
translation:
교수: 수렴 진화는 서로 무관한 유기체들이 동등한 환경적 압력에 노출되었을 때 어떻게 독립적으로 놀랍도록 유사한 생리적 적응을 진화시키는지 보여줍니다. 돌고래와 상어의 유선형 방추형 체형은 해양 환경에서 유체역학적 최적화를 보여주는 고전적인 형태학적 증거입니다.
질문: 돌고래와 상어 사이의 형태학적 유사성은 무엇을 예증하는가?
tip: "Convergent evolution"과 "unrelated organisms independently evolve strikingly similar adaptations"를 핵심 정답 선지와 일치시킵니다.
